options.text: ✅ It looks great, I can order with confidence
options.explanation: WARNING! This site shows many red flags. Never trust appearances alone.

options.text: 😂 This is ridiculous, the prices are impossible
options.explanation: Exactly! Discounts of -86% to -92% are impossible for new authentic products.

options.text: 🔓 The site doesn't use HTTPS correctly
options.explanation: Well spotted! The fake SSL badge and suspicious domain (.biz) are warning signs.

options.text: 💰 The prices are suspicious (discounts of -86% to -92%)
options.explanation: Bravo! iPhone for €199, MacBook for €399, Labubu for €12... this is clearly a scam.
Excellent instinct! All clues point to a fraud attempt.

options.text: ⭐ The reviews look fake (Marie D., Jean L., perfect ratings)
options.explanation: Perfect! Generic reviews with perfect scores are a classic sign of fraud.

options.text: ⏰ The timer and urgency alerts are suspicious
options.explanation: Very good! Artificial urgency is a manipulation technique to force impulse buying.

excellent.title: 🏆 Expert Cyber-Detective!
excellent.message: Congratulations! You've identified all the traps on this fake site. You're now an expert in detecting online fraud!
excellent.advice: Always keep checking sites before buying. When in doubt, ask an adult.

good.title: 👍 Good Detective!
good.message: Well done! You spotted most of the traps. With a bit more attention, you'll be an expert!
good.advice: Remember: if it's too good to be true, it's probably a scam.

average.title: 📚 Learning
average.message: Not bad, but there are still traps you didn't spot. Keep practicing!
average.advice: Take time to analyze details: prices, reviews, contact information, artificial urgency...

poor.title: ⚠️ Danger Alert!
poor.message: You fell for the trap! This site is a scam. Fortunately, this was just an exercise.
poor.advice: IMPORTANT: NEVER buy from a site with impossible prices, suspicious reviews, or without clear legal information.

missions.title: 🔒 Find the fake SSL badge
missions.explanation: This 'SSL Secured' badge in the header is fake. A real SSL certificate displays in the browser's address bar.

missions.title: 💰 Spot an impossible price
missions.explanation: A discount of more than 80% on new products is impossible. This is a classic trap of fraudulent sites.

missions.title: ⭐ Identify a fake review
missions.explanation: Reviews with generic names (Marie D., Jean L.) and perfect scores are suspicious.

missions.title: 📞 Find suspicious contact info
missions.explanation: No phone number, no physical address, SIRET 'pending'... A legal site must have this information.

missions.title: ⏰ Detect artificial urgency
missions.explanation: The resetting timer and fake alerts create pressure to buy without thinking.

missions.title: 📦 Find suspicious shipping
missions.explanation: 'European warehouse via China' with 15-30 day delivery is very suspicious for supposedly in-stock products.

missions.title: 🖼️ Spot stolen images
missions.explanation: Getty Images, Shutterstock watermarks prove the images are stolen and not real product photos.

advanced_mode.subtitle: Buy buttons are ACTIVE. One click = Game Over!

clues.title: Fake SSL badge in header
clues.description: The 'SSL Secured' badge is misleading. A real certificate displays in the URL.

clues.title: Suspicious domain name (.biz)
clues.description: Fraudulent sites often use less common extensions.

clues.title: Impossible iPhone price (-86%)
clues.description: €199 for an iPhone 16 Pro Max worth €1449? Impossible for new.

clues.title: Impossible MacBook price (-87%)
clues.description: €399 for a MacBook Pro M4 worth €2999? Pure scam.

clues.title: Impossible PS5 price (-82%)
clues.description: €99 for a PS5 worth €549? Too good to be true.

clues.title: Ridiculous Labubu prices (-87% to -92%)
clues.description: Labubu for €12 or €24? Real ones cost 10x more.

clues.title: Watermarks on images
clues.description: Getty Images, Shutterstock: the photos are stolen.

clues.title: Fake reviews with generic names
clues.description: Marie D., Jean L., Sophie T. with perfect scores = fake.

clues.title: Timer that resets
clues.description: The countdown restarts indefinitely to create urgency.

clues.title: Artificial stock alerts
clues.description: 'Only 3 left in stock!' is randomly generated.

clues.title: No phone number
clues.description: A real e-commerce site always has reachable customer service.

clues.title: SIRET 'pending'
clues.description: A legal site already has its SIRET before selling.

clues.title: Outdated bank logo
clues.description: The dated payment logo betrays an unprofessional site.
